meta.title: Parelcha Raja - Nare Park
meta.institution: Parel Vibhag Sarvajanik Ganeshotsav Mandal, Nare Park
meta.location: Bhivajirao Nare Udyan, Nare Park, Parel East, Mumbai
meta.foundedNote: Institutional account corroborated by 2017 and 2022 reporting.
meta.intro: Parelcha Raja here means the Nare Park festival of Parel Vibhag Sarvajanik Ganeshotsav Mandal. Its institutional history traces the celebration to ordinary mill workers in 1947. The standing Ganesh form, changing devotional interpretations and community initiatives distinguish its documented record. It must not be confused with Parelcha Maharaja, Parelcha Samrat or Parel Post Galli’s Vighnaharta, all separate organizations in the same broad neighborhood.

paragraphs.text: The institutional account dates the festival to 1947 and describes ordinary Parel mill workers gathering at Nare Park. Times of India independently reports the same start year. This supports a specific labor-neighborhood origin, without treating every later programme as something present from the first celebration.

sections.title: Standing forms that change with the year

paragraphs.text: Indian Express describes a standing tradition interpreted through Vishnu, Shiva and Rama. Its 2022 report names that year’s form Gajalaxmi and explains a foldable crown for passing beneath Lalbaug Bridge. The reported idol and bridge heights belong to that account, not a permanent surveyed specification.

Mumbai Mirror’s 2016 Nare Park report describes a Kaliya Mardan composition on a many-hooded serpent. The contrast with 2022 and the orange-clad standing figure in the specifically captioned 2025 photograph shows a changing repertoire. A generic image labeled only Parel is insufficient to establish which local mandal it depicts.

In 2017 the mandal announced it would stop seeking donations from nearby hawkers, with trustee Milind Gawde describing the burden of multiple festival requests. The report also mentions schoolbags, village-school computers, tree planting and blood donation. This gives a dated view of how a neighborhood institution negotiates its funding and service work.

For 2026, FPJ quotes treasurer Suresh Arondekar on a Pandharpur/Warkari setting and the use of Chandrabhaga water. That report’s illustration is labeled file photo, so it is not accepted here as a dated 2026 photograph. A current article date does not establish the capture year of its illustration.

The Nare Park archive gives a more specific visual record than a locality-only Parel caption. A 1971 print identifies a Krishna tableau; year-labelled arrival albums then show a rearing horse in 2014, an armed standing form in 2015, a serpent-supported 2016 idol and the multi-figure 2017 composition. The 2016 and 2017 photographs themselves carry the mandal name and year. Individual artists are left unassigned where the source does not name them.

The 2018 addition concerns padyapujan and preparations, so it does not stand in for a missing finished-idol portrait. A small native 2019 arrival frame preserves another form, while the 2026 album documents the turbaned, drum-bearing Warkari image discussed in contemporary reporting. Scene photographs, archive frames and annual captions establish different kinds of evidence and are retained as such.

years.title: Pandemic plans and online worship
years.summary: The Nare Park mandal announced a three-foot idol in place of its usual 23-foot installation. It planned immersion in an artificial tank, without a procession or neighbourhood fundraising. During the festival, a trustee described online darshan and health precautions.

claims.text: The Nare Park mandal began in 1947 and describes mill-worker origins.
The standing tradition was interpreted as Gajalaxmi in 2022.
Hawker donation collections stopped in 2017 according to the trustee’s announcement.

researchNotes.coverage: Independent exact-institution history and two visually inspected photo years. Generic 2016 Parel image rejected as insufficiently identified. Phase 2 examined 35 old-memory objects and samples from seven official annual albums, adding eight photo years including the explicitly printed 1971 Nare Park scene. All originals preserved unchanged.
gaps: Old-memory filenames such as 2002/2005/2006/2008/2009 are not item-level capture proof; several show differing forms and are withheld pending dated captions.
The 1979 paired image is a composite and not counted as a single documentary photo.
Official albums include unrelated scenery and at least one differently framed idol view; selected annual images are individually checked.
